on reading, something I didnt understand when younger

a lot of times, the "best" book for u to read next...will actually be a re-read.

age/wisdom/experience unlock parts of books that u missed. u will realize this more and more, over and over, as u get older

example being: every 5 years, you are prob best off just re-reading buffett/munger top to bottom

but even last week, I was going thru those Market Wizards books and posting quotes

I "read" all those at age 25-30 and have been operating under the assumption, okay, I've read the major investing canon

that assumption is busted, I need to scrap it

the "every 5 years" or "every 10 years" at the very most...that probably applies for EVERYTHING you have ever read.

the toggles and adjustments to make are:
1. there are far fewer great books than u think
2. you know far less than you think
3. what you thought you "read," you only digested some tiny % of it, and that % shrinks as time passes.

and this means entirely scrapping the "cocktail party" mentality of reading/books...reading whats new or reading as a social activity

fuck all of that

"I'm reading the book of Ecclesiastes for the 500th time" is prob the best answer

"I'm reading Market Wizards for the 8th time" will prob take u much farther than reading whatever the f is new...nothing is new esp in markets

that PTJ excerpt below, in one page, is probably equal to everything that has been written on trading/risk management in the past 25 years...it's almost LOLworthy

and every 5-10 years, u will understand that page at a deeper level.

think the point is clear

I just think abt this principle all the time, bc I have like 10 "books I haven't read" sitting on my desk, versus 2-3 that I want to re-read (lord chesterfield's letters, plutarch's moralia, montaigne's essays)

gut says highest/best use of time is the latter, and I think if u really observe how someone like Munger went about reading, it was this exact way.

u dont need to know everything, u just need the 100 best "mental models" or whatever u want to call them, and trust that those will be what carries u thru life...
